scope: projectable HMT gravitational constrained sector only; no DSIR; no matter-interface coefficient selection
scientific_question: On a fixed flat projectable HMT background, what is the linearized distributional Poisson-bracket kernel C12(x,y)={Phi1II(x),Phi2II(y)}, and for which lambda and Fourier modes is that local kernel nondegenerate?

source_locked_input.reference: J. Kluson, Hamiltonian Analysis of U(1) Invariant F(R) Horava-Lifshitz Gravity, arXiv:1012.0473
source_locked_input.linear_F_limit: F'(A)=1 (equivalently F(x)=x after auxiliary-field reduction), whose remaining Hamiltonian structure is identified with non-relativistic covariant/projectable HMT Hořava-Lifshitz gravity

constraints.Phi1II: (1/kappa^2) sqrt(g) G(R); for the flat audit take G'(0)=1 and choose the constant term so the flat background obeys G(0)=0
constraints.Phi2II_flat_linear_part: c_lambda nabla^2 pi with c_lambda=(1-lambda)/(D*lambda-1); curvature-times-momentum terms vanish to first order about R_ij=0, pi^ij=0

frozen_background.topology: flat T^3 with periodic boundary conditions
frozen_background.zero_mode_policy: k=0 is explicitly excluded from local invertibility claims and remains a separate global/zero-mode question

frozen_derivation_checks: derive delta R = partial_i partial_j h_ij - partial^2 h on the frozen flat background
derive {delta R(x),pi(y)}=(1-D) partial^2 delta(x-y), pi=delta_ij pi^ij
derive C12(x,y)=((1-D)/kappa^2)*((1-lambda)/(D*lambda-1))*partial^4 delta(x-y) up to the explicitly tracked Poisson/Fourier sign convention
for D=3 derive the nonzero-mode Fourier symbol proportional to -2*(1-lambda)/(kappa^2*(3*lambda-1))*k^4 up to the same tracked sign convention
classify generic lambda != 1,1/3 and k!=0 separately from lambda=1, lambda=1/3, and k=0
do not hide or regularize a lambda=1 rank change by selecting a convenient lambda after seeing the result

allowed: PASS_SCOPED if the exact linearized algebra reproduces the frozen bi-Laplacian kernel and its rank classification
report that generic lambda != 1,1/3 has a nonzero local Fourier symbol for k!=0 if derived
report that lambda=1 makes this particular flat linearized kernel vanish if derived
forbidden: claim that lambda=1 HMT is inconsistent, nonrenormalizable, or ruled out
claim that the full Faddeev-Senjanovic determinant has been computed
claim that the full HMT one-loop problem is evaluable
import ordinary projectable-Horava beta functions into HMT
change any previously frozen RTK threshold

critical_cases.lambda_equals_1: must be reported independently; vanishing of the flat linearized Phi2II Laplacian coefficient is a rank/evaluability issue for this kernel only
critical_cases.lambda_equals_1_over_3: critical DeWitt-metric denominator; excluded from the generic formula and requires a separate constrained analysis
critical_cases.k_equals_0: global zero mode; no local invertibility claim
